From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@cascadehealth.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch weekend capacity / temporary SLA ask

Grace —

Thanks again for the onboarding help. We’re planning a phased roll‑out of the pilot next Friday (6/25) that will send a short burst of traffic for customer enrollments and initial health checks. Our engineering lead estimates peak QPS could be ~2.5x the current test profile for a ~12‑hour window; afterwards volume will settle to baseline.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood temporarily raise our rate tier (burst allowance) for the first 72 hours of launch? We don’t expect the elevated traffic to continue after the window.
- If possible, can we get an SLA note for 95th percentile latency during that window, and explicit fallback behavior if we hit fairness throttling? Our product team needs this commitment for internal launch sign‑off.

I attached the launch mutual action plan + traffic forecast. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through details.

Best,
Alex
Director, Platform Engineering — Cascade Health
Attachments: CascadeHealth_Launch_MAPP.pdf (pdf, 220KB)
From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@cascadehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch weekend capacity / temporary SLA ask

Alex —

Thanks for the clear brief and the MAPP — this is doable with a few conditions so we can protect other customers and our SLOs. Proposed approach:

1) Temporary burst uplift: emergency +50% burst allowance for the first 72 hours (starting at your launch time). We can push to +100% only if you accept a short grace policy (we will apply soft fairness limits after sustained load >30m).
2) SLA addendum for launch window: Redwood will target 95th pct latency <= 350ms for text generation calls to the pinned model variant. This will be recorded as a short-term addendum and tied to the specific time window and traffic shape in your MAPP.
3) Fallback behavior: if sustained throttling occurs due to cross-customer fairness, traffic will be routed to a compatible lower‑cost variant with equivalent functional output; we’ll tag responses with X-Redwood-Fallback and provide metrics.

Action items:
- Can your team confirm the exact UTC launch start and timezone?
- I’ll loop in Legal & Billing to draft a 72‑hour SLA amendment and an updated invoice for the uplift.

Propose 30m call today at 3pm PT if that works — I can include Rishi (ops) and Laura (contracts).

—Grace
Grace O’Connor
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
